packs.title: Bay, Arts and Wild Places
packs.promise: Explore Sarasota through separate art, garden, coast and nature outings.

q.s: Notice how a living collection displays epiphytes.
st: Check current garden admission or use the official Downtown campus plant descriptions.
Find one orchid, bromeliad or other epiphyte display feature and its supporting structure.
Describe how the display differs from an ordinary ground planting without claiming a bloom is present today.

q.s: Observe conservation without chasing a bird.
st: Treat Osprey as a separate southbound trip; check current trail and entrance status.
Find one scrub or pine habitat feature on an open route or official park page.
Connect that feature to the park's scrub-jay conservation role without requiring a bird sighting.

q.s: Compare a built beach edge with a natural one.
st: Take the Bay Runner or plan separate transport; check beach and pavilion notices.
From a public beach approach, select one pavilion or shade structure and one shoreline form.
Sketch how the built and natural edges meet; do not enter the pool or water.

packs.title: Downtown and Bayfront on Foot
packs.promise: Follow downtown art, civic places and bayfront paths on foot.

q.s: Choose a public waterfront rest point.
st: Use an open park path and stay back from the marina and water edge.
Find one planted or shaded feature and one long view over the bay.
Choose a turn-back point if heat, rain or an event changes the route.
From open public paths, count the approaches around the park without stepping into traffic.
Choose two different directions a walker might take toward culture or the waterfront.
Draw a small route fork and note which marked crossing each choice needs.

q.s: Read one historic person through a public square.
st: Use or reveal the clue from open public space or the city's park description.
Find a fountain or historical-marker feature and one way the square connects nearby streets.
Explain what the marker says about Owen Burns without inventing an unlisted achievement.
